notes: Re-review on DotE5m2ChunkLoss at gate 752f03b36e81309e. assumption:dot is Rules.Num.DotE5m2ChunkLoss P. num.md lists it for an fp8 x fp8 tl.dot into float32 at maxImpreciseAcc 2^30, any precision, as the alternative to DotE5m2Chunk. It is DotF8ChunkLoss P .f8e5 .f8e5: for every precision, DotChunkLoss on the model's configuration with rho = 2^-7, sigma = 2^-12, alpha = 2^-126, kappa = 2, rho' = 2^-12 (printed in work/names6.lean). Its docstring says what the fact says. spec: errAt's step (1 + sigma)*E + min(rho*(X + E), kappa*A + rho'*(X + E)) + sigma*|S'| + alpha, with X = max(|S_j|, m_j) and A = chunkAbs, is what the fact gives per chunk. Take M = max(|S_j| + E_j, m_j) <= X + E; both arms grow with M; |s + c| <= |S'| + E (chunk_step). The fact's chunkAbs8 of step t's chunk c equals the loop's chunkAbs at 2t + c, with disabled lanes 0 (hca). This is the library's errM. The tolerance is explicit and computable. zero_rejected, drop_rejected and tol_spike keep it meaningful at every covered K. I recomputed every README figure exactly in rationals: spike at K - 1 0.806% at 512 and 4096; worst 71713*2^-23 = 0.855% attained at K = 4033 (K mod 64 = 1); pair input 0.0268 -> 0.0165 and 0.0658 -> 0.0175; one product at 0 13.70% -> 1.547% and 179.30% -> 7.253%; all ones 6.30% and 73.91%, second arm never the smaller; first chunk 1s then 1/16s (row and column) 12.46% -> 11.83% and 142.68% -> 73.73%; the x = y = 1.25 bounds below 0.015 and 0.014. On torch.randn data cast to float8e5 (my own draws: 2 x 20 and 200) the second arm is never the smaller, so the old and new tolerance agree exactly. The medians over 200 draws are 1.51 at K = 512 and 48 against a median |S| of 42 at K = 4096, the same order as the README's 1.5 and 52. All six theorems use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Non-blocking: OutSpec's docstring still says E comes from the exact partial sums and each chunk's largest lifted product; it now also depends on each chunk's exact magnitude, as tol's docstring says. The README's 'below |S| on half the draws' at K = 4096 holds of its 20 draws; over my 200 draws it held on about 40%.
